title: Jurgen Klopp shuts down Real Madrid rumours, but ‘not quite finished’ in coaching
content:
Jurgen Klopp has kept the door open for a future return to management by saying he is “not quite finished as a coach yet”.

Klopp, 58, has been Red Bull’s global head of soccer since January 2025 but has been consistently linked to coaching jobs following his exit from Liverpool in 2024. After rumours linking him to Real Madrid in January, he told The Athletic that he is “completely at peace with where I am” and doesn’t want to be anywhere else.

Speaking to reporters at an event in Germany on Monday he again called that idea “all nonsense” but left the door open to a return in the future.

“If Real Madrid had called, we would have heard about it by now,” he told MagentaTV. “But that’s all nonsense. They didn’t even call once. They didn’t even call my agent.”

Asked if he would consider coaching the German national team, he continued: “I’ve said that a thousand times already, but of course I’m not thinking about it at all right now.

“And as for the future, I’m not quite finished as a coach yet. So who knows what might come up in the next few years. But there are absolutely no plans in that regard.”

Klopp confirmed that he is “not thinking of throwing in the towel” with Red Bull, as he enters only his second year with the company, whose network is comprised of Bundesliga club RB Leipzig, Austria’s Red Bull Salzburg, New York Red Bulls in the United States, Red Bull Bragantino in Brazil and RB Omiya Ardija in Japan.

Its CEO of corporate projects and investments also ruled out the idea of a departure in a statement to The Athletic in February. Oliver Mintzlaff called reports of Klopp leaving to coach at either club or international level “complete nonsense and totally unfounded”.

“He invests a great deal, is in constant communication with our coaches and sporting directors, and is sustainably developing our Red Bull football philosophy,” he continued.

“We are convinced that he is the right man for the job. That’s where we are focusing all our energy and attention.”

Klopp joined Red Bull after nearly nine years at Liverpool, where he won the Premier League in the 2019-20 season and the Champions League the term before. He announced his departure in 2024 saying he was “running out of energy” and that he “cannot do the job again and again”.

His agent Marc Kosicke claimed in February that Manchester United and Chelsea had made approaches for him after he left, but both clubs denied doing so.

The German had previously had spells in charge of Mainz and Borussia Dortmund, where he won two Bundesliga titles.
